category: Version and update control for the apps of a self-hosted Nextcloud instance: an admin tool that lists every published version of an installed app from the App Store and from Git forges (GitHub, Codeberg), installs any older or newer version with pre-flight, migration and checksum guards, pins versions and detects drift, runs per-app automatic update policies inside a maintenance window behind a global kill switch, correlates installed versions with security advisories, and keeps an audit trail. It competes with the platform's own app management and update notifications, with dependency update bots (Renovate, Dependabot), with vulnerability scanners that match versions against advisory feeds (OSV-Scanner), and with in-platform update managers of other plugin ecosystems (Easy Updates Manager for WordPress).

capabilities.name: See every installed app with its installed version in one list.
capabilities.note: The Apps tab lists every enabled app as a card, but the card shows name, id and description only; the installed version the API already returns (installedVersion) appears only after 'Choose app' opens the detail. No single list of apps with their versions. Existing 2026-09-27: openspec/changes/archive/2026-06-14-move-to-admin-settings specifies the missing half; the code lacks it (defect of that change, not filed). See openspec/parity/gap-decisions.json.

evidence.nextcloud: apps/appstore/src/views/AppstoreManage.vue:33 (Installed category) with the version column at apps/appstore/src/components/AppTable/AppTableRow.vue:79; CLI core/Command/App/ListApps.php:64 prints installed versions.
evidence.renovate: lib/workers/repository/package-files.ts:39 renders a "Detected Dependencies" section in the dependency dashboard listing every detected dependency with its current version per package file; an "app" maps to a dependency.
evidence.dependabot: Closed service: the dependency graph lists every dependency of a repository with its version, and the Dependabot tab lists the monitored manifests (https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/how-tos/secure-your-supply-chain/secure-your-dependencies/explore-dependencies, https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/how-tos/secure-your-supply-chain/manage-your-dependency-security/list-configured-dependencies). Core: each ecosystem's file parser reads the declared versions, e.g. composer/lib/dependabot/composer/file_parser.rb. An app maps to a dependency in a manifest.
evidence.osv-scanner: An app maps to a package in a lockfile, SBOM or image. ,all-packages with ,format json lists every package with its version (cmd/osv-scanner/internal/helper/flags.go:182, docs/usage.md:125-135).
evidence.easy-updates-manager: includes/MPSUM_Plugins_List_Table.php:110-137 builds the Plugins tab from get_plugins() and includes/MPSUM_Plugins_List_Table.php:620-623 prints each plugin's installed version (Themes tab the same in includes/MPSUM_Themes_List_Table.php); an app maps to a plugin or theme. WordPress core Plugins screen lists them too.

evidence.nextcloud: apps/appstore/src/views/AppstoreManage.vue:39 lists apps with a pending update under the Updates category; counter from apps/appstore/lib/Controller/PageController.php:84 via Installer::isUpdateAvailable (lib/private/Installer.php:361).
evidence.renovate: lib/workers/repository/dependency-dashboard.ts:500-610 lists pending, awaiting-schedule, rate-limited and open update branches per dependency, and each available update becomes a branch or PR.
evidence.dependabot: Core: an available update surfaces only as an open pull request per dependency, "Bumps X from A to B" (common/lib/dependabot/pull_request_creator/message_builder.rb:452); closed service: no single list of outdated dependencies, and an org-wide dashboard is an open request (https://github.com/dependabot/dependabot-core/issues/2936).
evidence.osv-scanner: Only vulnerable packages get a Fixed Version column (docs/output.md:29); there is no general outdated-package report, and the hidden experimental update command bumps manifest dependencies without listing them first (cmd/osv-scanner/update/command.go:27-29).

The EUM tab itself does not print the new version.

capabilities.name: See where each installed app came from: the app store, a Git forge or a manual upload.

built.reachedOn: Apps tab (every app card) and Sources tab

capabilities.note: Every app card names its bound source (App Store, github:owner/repo, forgejo:owner/repo) from boundSourceId in the list payload. It is the binding, not provenance: an unbound app reads App Store even if it was installed by hand or from git, and manual upload is not a source kind.

evidence.nextcloud: The table row shows name, version, level and groups only (apps/appstore/src/components/AppTable/AppTableRow.vue:62-110); the store/git distinction exists internally (apps/appstore/lib/Controller/ApiController.php:341, lib/private/Installer.php:407) but is never shown. Nextcloud has only one install source, the app store.
evidence.renovate: Every dependency carries a datasource (lib/modules/datasource/types.ts), shown in the deprecations table (lib/workers/repository/dependency-dashboard.ts:476) and PR tables, but the detected-dependencies list groups by manager and file, not by source.
evidence.dependabot: Core: each dependency requirement carries its source (registry or git URL) and PR bodies link the source repository (common/lib/dependabot/pull_request_creator/message_builder/metadata_presenter.rb:98); closed service: the dependency graph shows the ecosystem but no per-dependency origin column (https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/how-tos/secure-your-supply-chain/secure-your-dependencies/explore-dependencies).
evidence.osv-scanner: Each finding shows the ecosystem and the lockfile or SBOM path it came from (docs/output.md:26-30), and Git-pinned dependencies get a pkg:git PURL (CHANGELOG.md:8-9); the registry or forge a package was fetched from is not shown.
evidence.easy-updates-manager: includes/MPSUM_Plugins_List_Table.php:617-646 shows version, author and plugin site, and a View details link only for plugins known to the wordpress.org API; nothing names where a plugin came from (directory, vendor updater or upload).

capabilities.name: See whether an app version is compatible with the running server version before choosing it.

built.reachedOn: Apps tab, version picker (Runs on this server / Not for this server version); occ versioniq:versions (Runs on this server column); GET /api/app/{appId}/versions (serverCompatible)

capabilities.note: Re-rated 2026-10-07 (parity scan), state and rating unchanged. The built half is specified in the version-management main spec (Fetch Available Versions: serverCompatible on each App Store version and on cached forge releases, shown in the web picker): App Store versions carry serverCompatible from platformVersionSpec, cached forge releases from their own info.xml, shown by ServerCompatBadge in the picker and as a column in occ versioniq:versions. The missing half stays specified in inventory-upgrade-readiness: a forge release that was never downloaded reads unknown, because the forge range lookup (ForgeRangeStore) is not built. Partial is the right rating until that lands.

evidence.nextcloud: apps/appstore/lib/Controller/ApiController.php:133-135 computes missingDependencies and isCompatible; shown in apps/appstore/src/components/AppstoreSidebar/AppDetailsTab.vue:137 and filterable via 'Show incompatible' (apps/appstore/src/components/AppToolbar.vue:105). Applies to the single latest release only.
evidence.renovate: lib/config/options/index.ts:499 constraintsFiltering filters releases by language constraints (engines, PHP), and lib/modules/datasource/nextcloud/readme.md has you point registryUrls at a per-platform apps.json so only releases for that server version are offered; not shown to the user as a compatibility verdict.
evidence.dependabot: Core: releases whose language requirement (e.g. the PHP or Python version) is not satisfied are filtered before a target is chosen (common/lib/dependabot/package/package_latest_version_finder.rb:228); the compatibility is enforced silently, not shown to the user for a version of their choice.
evidence.osv-scanner: not checked: the row has no counterpart in a lockfile, SBOM and image scanner, and neither the source at v2.6.0 nor the docs settle it either way (no concept of a platform version a package must be compatible with).
evidence.easy-updates-manager: WordPress core shows "Compatible/Untested with your version of WordPress" and requirement details in View details (https://wordpress.org/documentation/article/manage-plugins/#plugin-compatibility-1); EUM Premium safe mode blocks updates that do not meet the WordPress or PHP requirement (premium, docs: https://easyupdatesmanager.com/knowledge-base/safe-mode-premium/).

built.reachedOn: Apps tab (app card marked Disabled, with an Enable button)

capabilities.note: The app list joins IAppManager::getEnabledApps() with getAppInstalledVersions(false), so installed but disabled apps are listed with a Disabled mark and their versions can be listed and installed from the page. The card's Enable button enables the app through Nextcloud's own OCS apps endpoint after a password prompt (#433).

evidence.nextcloud: The Disabled category lists disabled apps (apps/appstore/src/views/AppstoreManage.vue:37), but the Updates view only offers updates for active apps (same file :39); occ app:update ,all covers disabled apps too (core/Command/App/Update.php:82).

evidence.dependabot: not checked: a manifest-based repository has no counterpart of an installed but disabled component; development and optional dependencies are the nearest analogue and are updated through the allow dependency-type option (https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/reference/supply-chain-security/dependabot-options-reference).
evidence.osv-scanner: not checked: the row has no counterpart in a lockfile, SBOM and image scanner, and neither the source at v2.6.0 nor the docs settle it either way (no enabled or disabled state for a package).
evidence.easy-updates-manager: includes/MPSUM_Plugins_List_Table.php:110-137 lists all installed plugins from get_plugins(), active or inactive, and each can be blocked or set to auto-update; WordPress core updates inactive plugins too (https://wordpress.org/documentation/article/dashboard-updates-screen/).

capabilities.note: Always-enabled apps get a CORE flag and can be hidden; every other shipped app gets a 'Shipped with Nextcloud' badge on its card, and an explanatory error when its versions are requested. Fixed in #438.

evidence.nextcloud: occ app:list ,shipped=true|false (core/Command/App/ListApps.php:31); the API marks shipped and internal apps (apps/appstore/lib/Controller/ApiController.php:136,465).
evidence.renovate: not checked: no clear analog in a repository dependency bot for components shipped with the platform versus installed separately.
evidence.dependabot: not checked: no counterpart of apps bundled with a server was found; direct versus transitive dependencies is the nearest analogue, which the dependency graph shows (https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/how-tos/secure-your-supply-chain/secure-your-dependencies/explore-dependencies).
evidence.osv-scanner: Image scans report the layer that introduced a package and the base image (docs/output.md:32-37, CHANGELOG.md:164), which separates base-image packages from ones added on top; source scans have no such split.
evidence.easy-updates-manager: WordPress bundles default themes, Akismet and Hello Dolly as ordinary plugins and themes with no marker; EUM rows (includes/MPSUM_Plugins_List_Table.php:483-646) carry no bundled flag. Must-use plugins are listed separately by core but are admin-installed (https://wordpress.org/documentation/article/manage-plugins/#must-use-plugins-1).

evidence.nextcloud: Every check reads the local instance's config and apps folders (lib/private/App/AppStore/Fetcher/Fetcher.php:130-204, lib/private/Installer.php:135); there is no remote-instance concept in the apps management or updatenotification code.
evidence.renovate: lib/config/options/index.ts:1197 autodiscover and lib/config/options/index.ts:1258 repositories run one bot across many repositories; Mend cloud adds an org view in the Developer Portal (docs/usage/mend-hosted/overview.md:26-31).

evidence.osv-scanner: One run scans many directories recursively, several lockfiles and SBOMs (cmd/osv-scanner/scan/source/command.go:28-50), or an image; there is no central view over several instances.
evidence.easy-updates-manager: Free handles a multisite network from one screen (network admin menu, includes/MPSUM_Admin.php:577); managing many separate sites needs UpdraftCentral, a separate product that EUM plugs into (includes/MPSUM_UpdraftCentral.php:13-40, https://easyupdatesmanager.com/knowledge-base/updraftcentral/).

capabilities.name: Verify the code signature of an app package before installing it.

built.evidence: lib/Service/SelectedReleaseInstallerService.php:133 (verifyCertificate: root chain, CRL, revoked serial, CN equals app id), lib/Service/SelectedReleaseInstallerService.php:604 (SHA-512 archive signature)

capabilities.note: App Store packages are checked against the Nextcloud code-signing root and CRL, the certificate CN must match the app id, and the archive signature is verified before files are swapped. Forge releases have no signature to verify and rely on SHA-256 instead.

evidence.nextcloud: downloadApp validates the certificate against the Nextcloud code signing root, checks the CRL and the CN against the app id, and verifies the SHA512 signature of the archive (lib/private/Installer.php:172-243,336).
evidence.renovate: No general signature verification; the PR body warns when the current npm release had an attestation and the new one has none (lib/workers/repository/update/pr/index.ts:142-156), and the hex datasource reads a signed registry (lib/modules/datasource/hex/v2/signed.ts).

evidence.osv-scanner: not checked: the scanner's own releases carry SLSA provenance (docs/installation.md:93-101), but verification of scanned or remediated package signatures was not found in the source or docs.
evidence.easy-updates-manager: WordPress core verifies Ed25519 signatures of core packages only and soft-fails; plugin packages are not signed (https://make.wordpress.org/core/2019/05/17/security-in-5-2/). EUM adds no signature check.

evidence.dependabot: not checked: lockfile integrity hashes are written by each package manager that Dependabot runs, not by Dependabot; I did not trace a Dependabot-owned record.

capabilities.name: Before a server upgrade, list the installed apps that do not support the PHP version the server will run on.

capabilities.note: The PHP constraint is only enforced after download and file swap during a real install, through the server's \OC_App::checkAppDependencies, which then reverts; the version list carries only version and changelog, so an admin cannot see beforehand which versions support the running PHP. Reworded 2026-09-27 to the gap updater issue 750 describes (list PHP-incompatible apps before a server upgrade); the old wording was "See whether an app version supports the running PHP version, not only the server version, before installing or upgrading.", which read broader than that issue. evidence.nextcloud: lib/private/App/AppStore/Fetcher/AppFetcher.php:88-106 drops store releases whose PHP spec does not match the running PHP_VERSION, and lib/private/App/DependencyAnalyzer.php:110-127 adds 'PHP %s or higher is required' to missingDependencies, shown in apps/appstore/src/components/AppstoreSidebar/AppDetailsTab.vue:137. The updater does not list PHP-incompatible apps before a server upgrade (updater issue 750 is open).
evidence.renovate: lib/modules/manager/composer/schema.ts:351-352 extracts the project's php constraint and lib/modules/datasource/packagist/schema.ts:123 records each release's php requirement; with constraintsFiltering strict (lib/config/options/index.ts:499, lib/modules/datasource/common.ts:178) incompatible releases are dropped silently. An app maps to a dependency; the constraint is the declared one, not a running PHP, and no verdict is shown.
evidence.dependabot: Core: common/lib/dependabot/package/package_latest_version_finder.rb:220-235 filters out releases whose language requirement (such as PHP) is not satisfied, and composer resolution runs with the repository's platform requirements (composer/lib/dependabot/composer/update_checker/version_resolver.rb:228). Enforced silently, logged only; an app maps to a dependency.
evidence.osv-scanner: internal/scalibrplugin/presets.go:34 only wires the composer.lock extractor for PHP; a search of cmd/, internal/ and pkg/ for php, engines and runtime constraints found no check of the runtime version a package release supports, and the output fields (docs/output.md:22-28) carry no compatibility data.

Decided no on 2026-09-28 (defer retired): no competitor rated yes, a feature request as demand, a feature request needs one competitor yes to build, outside the core areas (area autoupdate). Reversible when a tender, a second competitor or a feature request with a competitor yes arrives.
